winning_case.argument: Yes, and anyone who watches him gets there before the spreadsheet does.

royce.claim: Cade is a top-10 player: voters and the standings back him, and he's still improving.
supports: Honors: two All-Star selections, voted over seasons (F4)
Team result: Pistons third in the East (F14)
Turn on Deacon's number: this season's true shooting beats Shai's and Jokic's at the same scope (F8, F25, F36)
royce.answer: The assist drop: he says last season's 9.9 is who Cade is and eight games is a small slice, using Deacon's own grace rule.

deacon.claim: Cade is a strong player but sits just outside the top 10, in the 11 to 15 range.
supports: Efficiency against the elite: true shooting this season and last (F8, F12) against Jokic's and Shai's last-season marks (F37, F26)
Playmaking: 7.6 assists with a 2.0 assist-to-turnover ratio against Jokic's 9.3 (F6, F9, F35)
Availability: never played every game in five full seasons (F3)
deacon.answer: The same-scope turn on true shooting: he concedes that eight games cuts both ways, then moves to the bigger samples.

lonnie.claim: Cade is top 10 because Detroit's offense runs through what he does as scorer and creator.
supports: Role: 24 points, 7.6 assists, 5.6 rebounds as the hub (F5, F6, F7)
Results tied to his role: Pistons 6-2 with a +9.4 differential (F13, F15)
Steady scoring: this season's points match last season's (F5, F10)
lonnie.answer: The assist drop is eight games from a player who was at 9.9, so it gets the same grace Deacon gives Shai.

beats: Opening positions: Lonnie on role, Royce on honors and the standings, Deacon on efficiency against the elite
Main clash: same-scope true shooting turns Deacon, then Lonnie traps him on grace for slow starts
Exposed weakness: the assist drop to 7.6 hits Royce and Lonnie, who answer with last season's 9.9 and the grace rule
Decisive exchange: availability, where last season's games played put Cade level with Luka, Wemby, and Jokic, and Deacon is left conceding the ground and holding only the 11-to-15 call
